title: Cohort Risk Scoring & Adaptive Gate Playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic working playbook for running cohort-driven, risk-scored canaries and adaptive gates for feature releases and A/B tests. It attempts to bridge product, SRE, and analytics responsibilities and provide a repeatable decision flow that minimizes manual firefighting. Drafted as a practical checklist + signal matrix rather than academic experiment design.

When to apply this playbook:
- New change impacts inference path (model, runtime, routing) or billing logic (batching/quantization)
- Non-trivial downstream effect expected on latency, token-cost, or error surface
- Changes touching private/dedicated customers, or features behind tiered routing

High-level flow (one-paragraph):
1) Identify affected cohorts (by org tier, region, route, model family).
2) Define risk score per cohort based on signal weights (latency, error-rate, quality regressions, cost delta, security sensitivity).
3) Pick initial exposure slices (micro-cohort -> small cohort -> graduated cohorts) with automatic rollback thresholds tied to risk score.
4) Run adaptive canary with continuous evaluation and explicit gates (auto-hold, notify, escalate).

Roles and responsibilities (cross-functional):
- Product owner: hypothesis, acceptance criteria, target cohorts, user-visible metrics.
- Eng rollout lead (console): config for routing, feature flag, rollout policy, and rollback execution.
- SRE: guardrail dashboards, alerts, automated mitigation (circuit breakers, capacity overrides).
- Analytics: metric definitions, SQL for cohort joins, continuous evaluation tasks.
- Security/compliance: sign-off when cohorts include regulated customers.

Signal matrix and scoring (example weights):
- P95 latency increase (30%) — direction: up — scoring: 0.0 (<=5%), 0.5 (5-15%), 1.0 (>15%)
- Error-rate (5xx or model failures) (25%) — scoring: 0.0 (<=0.1%), 0.5 (0.1-0.5%), 1.0 (>0.5%)
- Quality delta (eval prompt set; BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) (20%) — scoring: 0.0 (<=1%), 0.5 (1-3%), 1.0 (>3%)
- Cost per token (15%) — scoring: 0.0 (<=3%), 0.5 (3-10%), 1.0 (>10%)
- Security/PII exposure flag (10%) — binary: 1.0 if triggers, else 0.0
Total risk score = weighted sum (range 0.0–1.0).

Risk-based exposure policy (example):
- Low risk (<=0.2): fast path: 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h if stable.
- Medium risk (0.2-0.6): conservative: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with 12h evaluation windows.
- High risk (>0.6): gated: internal-only or shadowed for at least 24h, manual sign-off required.

Automated gates and actions (per cohort evaluation window):
- If any single signal crosses "critical" threshold (e.g. P95 > +30% or error-rate >1%), trigger automatic rollback and notify on-call via Slack + PagerDuty runbook.
- If total risk score increases by >0.2 between windows, hold progression and create an incident review ticket (PROJ-4217 pattern).
- Soft alerts: email to product/analytics for intermediate degradations; escalate if sustained >2 windows.

Minimum monitoring dashboard (SRE + Analytics):
- Cohort selector dropdown and cohort size/time-series
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) separated by model/route
- Error-rate by error class + stack traces link
- Quality evals: holdout prompt set pass rate and sample outputs (red/amber/green)
- Cost delta per 1M tokens and estimated monthly run-rate impact
- Traffic routing counts and failover incidents

Communication templates (short):
- Pre-rollout (Slack): "Rolling out X to cohort A (1%). Hypothesis: improved cost by 8% with no quality regression. Watch latency P95 and error-rate. Contact @eng-rollout for questions."
- Auto-rollback notification: "AUTO-ROLLBACK: X -> cohort A. Trigger: p95 +32% at 12:14 UTC. Action: rollback executed; incident ticket created: PROJ-4319. Owners: @SRE, @Product."

Experiment matrix to set up (example):
- Axis 1: cohort (internal, beta orgs, small/medium/large customers)
- Axis 2: variant (control, new-routing, quantized-model, caching-on)
- Axis 3: metric buckets (latency, errors, cost, quality)
- Required sample sizes: use pragmatic thresholds (min 500 requests / cohort or time-bound 4 hours) rather than strict power calc for platform-release canaries.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm target cohorts and exclude list (PII/regulatory)
- [ ] Define primary alarm triggers + thresholds; register alerts
- [ ] Create evaluation queries and golden dataset for quality checks
- [ ] Configure rollout policy and automated rollback rules in console
- [ ] Add stakeholders to the rollout channel and schedule 1hr watch window
- [ ] Ensure canary telemetry retention for debug (retain logs for 7 days)

Post-rollout retrospective items:
- Capture any near-misses and update signal weights if noisy
- Record manual interventions and time-to-detect metrics
- Update runbook snippets and add any automation we needed to do manually

Open questions / decisions to make (working):
- Do we standardize on the weighted score above or allow product teams to tune weights per launch? (tradeoff: consistency vs. domain sensitivity)
- How do we surface qualitative regressions in near-real-time without overloading reviewers? (sampling + automated semantic similarity may help)
- Can we centralize cohort definitions (single source of truth) so analytics and rollout configs match?

Quick links / snippets:
- SQL sample for cohort join: SELECT request_id, org_id, variant, latency_ms FROM requests WHERE timestamp >= ... (analytics to finalize)
- Example PagerDuty escalation: GOV-Prod-Oncall -> Eng-Rollout-Pager -> Product-Owner

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a lightweight UI mock for console: per-cohort risk score widget + "suggested exposure" button
- Sync with Solutions Eng about private deployment cohorts (next Thurs)
- Run a tabletop with SRE + Analytics on a simulated high-error rollback (date: 2025-02-20)

Appendix (short):
- Historical incident tiebacks: examples where cost regressions were missed because rollout didn’t track cost delta (link to postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/pm-2024-07-cost-spike)

This document is intentionally informal. Feedback welcome — ping in #prod-console or add comments inline.
